hypotheses.justification: The morphism s := (L.one (𝟙 (Spec K))).1 : Spec K ⟶ A satisfies s ≫ f = 𝟙 (field .2 of SchemeHomOver), so s is a section of f. Separatedness is not needed because the base Spec K is a one-point space. Mathlib's `isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id {X Y : Scheme} [Subsingleton Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) (hg : g ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) : IsClosedImmersion g` (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean) proves exactly this. Its proof is local on X: on an affine open Spec R containing the image point, the map R → K has a left inverse, so it is surjective and gives a closed immersion; on an affine open missing the point, the preimage is empty and the map is trivially a closed immersion. The Subsingleton instance holds because the points of Spec (CommRingCat.of K) are PrimeSpectrum K, which has `instance [Field R] : Unique (PrimeSpectrum R)` (RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Basic.lean). Spec K is nonempty, so there is no other degenerate case. The replacement proof is `isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id f _ (L.one _).2`, possibly with an explicit `haveI : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))`. It replaces the step `IsClosedImmersion.of_comp`, the only place IsSeparated f was used. I checked this lemma in current Mathlib master but could not check the library's own Mathlib version; if the lemma is missing there, the affine-cover argument above can be written out directly.
